I'm mapping out the object categories and tracing the dapib dependency chain that links boxud's items together in sequence.

The chain runs fagup→cahuf→bunew→firix→ramim→lomic→sofiv→qizez. The sukaw action shifts voqev(hivos, pepux) to voqev(hivos, weful) whenever dapib(weful, pepux) holds, essentially stepping voqev one link earlier in the chain, and I'm using this to figure out how to get laref from qizez to sofiv.

Since dapib(sofiv, qizez) already exists, laref only needs one sukaw application. But cihav needs to move all the way from qizez to firix, which requires four successive applications (qizez→sofiv→lomic→ramim→firix), each time shifting the pepux/weful pair one step further back along the chain.

I'm also checking the remaining preconditions — butim ruraq wujum is satisfied by ruraq being nixam or nelid and wujum being nozuc, and now I'm working out the guvid hivos ruraq noweb condition.

I'm noticing a potential issue: for laref, noweb starts at qizez, but qizez never appears as the first argument in any dapib fact, so there's no valid jebas — meaning that direction of the chain doesn't work as I assumed, and I need to re-examine which argument order dapib actually uses.

Right, so sukaw is inapplicable when noweb=qizez since qizez has no outgoing dapib edge - that fact just doesn't exist. This means I need to first use verun or qajec to shift guvid/regum/jobaq away from qizez before sukaw can apply, freeing noweb to be something with an actual dapib target. Let me re-check the sukaw parameters more carefully: it needs dapib(noweb,jebas) and dapib(weful,pepux) to both hold given the current guvid and voqev bindings.

Trying verun next: guvid target is pepux=qizez which works since dapib(sofiv,qizez) exists, so weful=sofiv is fine. But regum's target noweb is also qizez initially, and dapib(qizez,jebas) still doesn't exist - so verun is blocked too, same underlying problem.

Wait, I realize butim's fuvif parameter needs a culig-type value, but initially nixam is mapped to nozuc which is a zekaz, not culig. So I need xuhex first to shift butim(nixam,...) to something culig-typed. Checking the sifos relations, sifos(nozuc,fawup) lets me apply xuhex(nixam,nozuc,fawup) to change butim from nixam-nozuc to nixam-fawup, and fawup is culig - that satisfies the precondition.

The same trick applies to nelid using xuhex(nelid,nozuc,fawup). But now I'm noticing sukaw needs a butim with a zekaz wujum (nozuc specifically), so if I convert both bixut away from nozuc I'll lose that requirement - I should keep at least one bixut on nozuc for sukaw, or exploit that sifos(nozuc,fawup) is symmetric so I can flip back and forth as needed. Now I'm sketching the sukaw call for the laref goal, since it only needs a single-step change from qizez to sofiv.

Working through preconditions, I realize both the guvid and regum values start at qizez, and there's no dapib(qizez, jebas) - so both the sukaw and verun paths I was considering are blocked right from the initial state, meaning I need to find a different action to get out of qizez first before either approach becomes viable.

I notice qajec might be the way out - since laref fawup's jobaq value is sofiv rather than qizez, and dapib(sofiv, jebas) does exist. This lets me advance jobaq and regum together via weful and jebas, breaking the deadlock at qizez.

Stepping back, this puzzle resembles a renamed IPC domain, and I should just model it abstractly as a graph. I'm treating each predicate as a pointer variable: guvid and regum tracking handler-object pairs across the boxud chain, jobaq covering the six handler-object pairs from init, and voqev tracking a per-handler value.

I'm mapping out the chain order for the eight elements and the butim relation linking positions to categories, then working through the verun action's effects -- it moves regum one step down the chain while moving guvid one step up, so I'm figuring out how these two pointers shift in opposite directions.

Now I'm tracing similar patterns for sukaw (guvid down, voqev up) and qajec (jobaq down, regum up), plus noting that xuhex handles edge transitions in the butim relation. Working toward the goal state where voqev needs to reach sofiv, which sits just one position above qizez in the chain.

For voqev cihav to reach firix, that's four steps up from qizez, so guvid needs to decrease correspondingly through sukaw actions - but since guvid starts at qizez (the bottom), it can't decrease at all initially, which means I need a different approach to build up the necessary preconditions before applying sukaw.

So the sequence has to be: verun first raises guvid up (drawing from regum decreasing), and only once guvid sits above qizez can sukaw then push it back down while pulling voqev upward. But regum is also stuck at qizez initially, so it needs its own boost via qajec first, which in turn depends on jobaq decreasing - and jobaq's starting values vary across the laref/cihav and bolob/cakam combinations, so I'm tracing through which of those pairs already have room to decrease versus which need their own upstream fix first.

Actually the increase step for regum doesn't have the same restriction as decreasing - since qizez has an incoming edge from sofiv, regum can rise from qizez just fine through qajec. The real constraint is on jobaq's decrease requirement, since jobaq starting at qizez has no outgoing edge, and that's the case for the laref-bolob combination specifically.

So checking each hivos combination, jobaq must not sit at qizez to decrease - laref-fawup works since jobaq starts at sofiv there, and both cihav paths work fine since their starting values allow decreasing. I'm now working out the toggling strategy using xuhex to flip butim relations back and forth between the two symmetric pairs, which gives enough flexibility to set up whichever culig each step needs.

With only two bixut resources holding butim values, mapping the sifos edges reveals a simple path structure connecting bolob-cakam-fawup-nozuc, meaning shifting from one end to the other takes three toggle steps through the middle nodes, all reversible. This tells me each increase to voqev requires first bumping guvid, which requires decreasing regum, which in turn requires regum being above the baseline value to begin with.

For laref specifically, I'm tracing the exact sequence needed to raise voqev by one step: first increase guvid via verun, then use that raised guvid value to power a sukaw step that pushes voqev up while returning guvid to baseline. But I hit a snag -- regum(laref,fawup) starts at baseline, so it can't be decreased directly; it needs to be raised first via qajec, which itself depends on decreasing jobaq.

So I lay out the order: use qajec to bump regum(laref,fawup) up to sofiv while jobaq drops to qizez, then use verun to raise guvid(laref,nixam) using that new regum value as the supporting condition.

Next I convert butim(nixam,fawup) into butim(nixam,nozuc) using xuhex along the direct sifos path, then apply sukaw to shift guvid(laref,nixam) back down while voqev(laref,qizez) becomes voqev(laref,sofiv), completing the chain of dependent state transitions.

Now I've achieved the target voqev(laref,sofiv). For the next goal, voqev(cihav,firix), I need four sequential increments from qizez through sofiv, lomic, ramim, to firix, so I'm planning to repeat a similar four-step process using cihav's jobaq reservoir and qajec's effect of decreasing jobaq by one adjacent link while increasing regum by one adjacent link.

Since each qajec call moves jobaq and regum independently along the fixed linear chain by one position each, I need jobaq(cihav,f) to decrease by four total positions to match the four regum increases required, so I'm now indexing the chain positions to figure out exactly how far jobaq(cihav,bolob) sits from qizez.

With the chain positions set, jobaq(cihav,bolob) at position 4 can decrease down to qizez at 7, giving up to 3 steps, while jobaq(cihav,cakam) and jobaq(cihav,fawup) at position 5 each give 2 steps, so the total available decrease across those three f-values is 7 steps. But I realize each qajec call ties jobaq(h,f,noweb) and regum(h,f,pepux) together under the same f index, so the decrease and increase must happen per matching f rather than being freely combinable across different f-values.

Since each call moves jobaq and regum one step apiece, chaining calls for a given f swaps their end positions symmetrically: for bolob, 3 calls bring regum up to ramim's original spot; for cakam and fawup, 2 calls each bring regum up to lomic's original spot.

Now I'm working out how verun links regum(h,f) decreases to guvid(h,r) increases — since r and f are independent, a single verun call can pull from any f as long as butim(r,f) currently holds, meaning guvid(h,r) can accumulate increases from multiple different f sources depending on how xuhex sets each r's butim value. I'm trying to figure out how to get the total guvid(cihav,r) increase up to 4, since voqev requires that much and sukaw ties the guvid decrease to voqev.

So the plan is to first push guvid(cihav,r) up by 4 (from qizez position 7 to position 3), then use sukaw calls to decrease guvid back down by 4 while increasing voqev correspondingly, with r fixed to a value whose wujum equals nozuc. To get regum(cihav,bolob) up to position 4, I increased it by 3 from qizez pos 7 — now I need to work out how decreasing regum(h,f) (moving it back toward qizez) interacts with increasing guvid via verun to supply the 4 total increases needed.

Working through the sources: bolob gives 3 available steps, cakam gives 2, fawup gives 2, totaling 7 when I only need 4 — so I can combine bolob's 3 steps with 1 step from cakam, or use cakam and fawup together for 4. Building regum(cihav,bolob) up to position 4 itself takes 3 qajec calls decreasing jobaq(cihav,bolob) through the chain, each needing adjacent dapib pairs to hold, which works since the chain is linear.

Building regum(cihav,cakam) up requires 1 qajec call moving jobaq(cihav,cakam) from lomic to sofiv, which correspondingly moves regum(cihav,cakam) from qizez to sofiv — then a verun call can shift that back to qizez while bumping guvid(cihav,r) by 1.

Now I want to lay out the actual position mapping (fagup=0 through qizez=7) and confirm voqev(cihav) needs to move from qizez(7) to firix(3), an increase of 4, which matches the guvid(cihav,r) requirement I'm assembling from these sources.

The plan converges: guvid(cihav,r) rises from qizez(7) to firix(3) via 4 verun calls, then 4 sukaw calls simultaneously walk guvid back from firix(3) to qizez(7) while voqev(cihav) drops from qizez(7) to firix(3) in lockstep — exactly matching the target movement.

The regum pool splits into 3 steps sourced from bolob and 1 step from cakam, together supplying the full 4-step guvid increase needed. Now I'm mapping the position chain explicitly (fagup through qizez) against the given dapib edges to confirm every single-step transition used in the walk actually exists.

I still need to work out the xuhex sequence to shift nelid's butim value through the bolob-cakam-fawup-nozuc chain so it holds the correct fuvif/wujum value at each stage: bolob for the qajec and verun calls, then cakam for one more each, then nozuc for the four sukaw calls, tracking exactly how many xuhex hops each transition costs.
